correctness.rationale: On the low gas branch F'=Phi'/z>0 and the dimensionless remaining gas mass is Phi(g). The interface flux is 1, its radius in y=chi|x| is log(m)/Q, and the interior liquid density is at least Q while the pure gas is below Q/2. Outside, the gas profiles differ in F by H, with H(1)=0 and H'=1/a-1/(Qm)>0, so they are strictly ordered in the opposite sense. Equal mass and the single sign switch give the unique equal-prior Bayes region up to null sets and TV=(Phi(z)-1)/m, where z is obtained on W_0. Implicit differentiation gives (Phi(z))'=z/a-z/(Qm), yielding G/m^2. In the a-coordinate 0<z_a<z/a, so z+(a+1-2z)z_a>0 in both sign cases and G strictly decreases from 1/q. At Q=5 the concave quadratic in z has maximum 49/16<5. At Q=20, F(6)<F(10)-log(5)/20<F(7): use log(5/3)>1/2 and log(5)<2 for the first inequality, and log(10/7)<=51/140 and log(5)>4/3 for the second, from the log atanh series. Thus G_*<0 for Q=20. At the fold F(a) has the terms -epsilon^2/2-epsilon^3/3, and analytic inversion at F'(z_*)>0 gives the stated negative cubic and hence D'' asymptotic to -z_*/(4 s^(5/2) sqrt(s-m)). The lower endpoint is regular with slope 1/q. Only the prescribed symmetric continuum profiles and one mass-normalized draw are involved. Notes and supplied script were inspected, not run. Separate bisection and split spatial quadrature at Q=20 give m_max approximately 4.8833131953 and TV approximately 0.6785991081, agreeing with quadrature to 7.1e-10 with the gas tail truncated at y=30; these are bounded corroborations.
